title: Temperature records by continent
measure: The highest and lowest air temperatures ever officially recorded in each region, in °C, as verified by the World Meteorological Organization. The WMO keeps records by region, so there are seven entries rather than ten. Ranked by highest temperature.

entries.name: North America
entries.note: The hottest temperature ever recorded on Earth, on 10 July 1913. Some weather historians doubt it, but the WMO still accepts it. The low was on 3 February 1947.
entries.source: World Meteorological Organization, Archive of Weather and Climate Extremes (July 2025)

entries.name: Africa
entries.note: High on 7 July 1931, low on 11 February 1935.
entries.source: World Meteorological Organization, Archive of Weather and Climate Extremes (July 2025)

entries.name: Asia
entries.note: High on 21 July 2016, measured to within 0.1 °C. The low was reached in 1892 and 1933.
entries.source: World Meteorological Organization, Archive of Weather and Climate Extremes (July 2025)

entries.name: South-West Pacific
entries.note: High on 2 January 1960, low on 17 July 1903.
entries.source: World Meteorological Organization, Archive of Weather and Climate Extremes (July 2025)

entries.name: South America
entries.note: High on 11 December 1905, low on 1 June 1907.
entries.source: World Meteorological Organization, Archive of Weather and Climate Extremes (July 2025)

entries.name: Europe
entries.note: High on 11 August 2021, the newest record here. Continental Europe only: the WMO's Europe region also covers Israel and Greenland, which hold 54.0 °C and −69.6 °C.
entries.source: World Meteorological Organization, Archive of Weather and Climate Extremes (July 2025)

entries.name: Antarctica
entries.location: Signy Research Station, South Orkney Islands
entries.note: The low of −89.2 °C, on 21 July 1983, is the coldest temperature ever recorded on Earth. On the Antarctic mainland the record high is 18.3 °C.
entries.source: World Meteorological Organization, Archive of Weather and Climate Extremes (July 2025)
